column4: S4.1: in the live A/B every C3 hook was on, so the original arm's sound.dll callees that had an SG_HOOK ran the shim's reimplementations, and arm 2 was the reimplementation; the replay runs the original callees and the original as arm 2. Equality with the CSV therefore also rests on those reimplementations having matched on the paths the live keys reached.
column5: Where a key disagrees with its CSV, replay it with the callees' reimplementations as second executors (KeyRun second_arm / machine_factory) to see whether a hooked callee explains it.

column4: S4.1: the CSVs print doubles in two ways: the 2026-10-07 runs (c3ar nextRandomFloat, c3au floatCopySign) the shortest form, the 2026-10-14 runs (c3fh _st0 keys) the exact decimal expansion cut after 17 significant digits. No sound.dll CSV between those dates returns a double, so the Frida upgrade date is not determined; TRUNC17_FROM is set to 2026-10-10.
column5: Find the Frida version in a log or pip history of the rounds between 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-13, or a jgld / exe CSV of that window returning a double.

column4: S4.1: a JS exception inside a NativeCallback: Frida reports it and the native caller continues; the value the call returns then is taken as 0 (eax 0, f 0). One key reaches it (Wave_Device::freeBufferList, c3fq's converter stub calls .toUInt32() on a number) and matches its CSV with 0.
column5: Read gumjs's native-callback invoke path for the Frida version of round 35, or provoke it in a live session.

column4: S4.1: cmdNode::scalarDeletingDtor 0x1000cc40 and WaveInDeviceBase_scalarDtor 0x1002a380 (c3dj_devfree, 2026-10-10T17:31 boot): the CSVs give the same state hash for flag bit 0 set and clear (distinct 5), so the live heap stand-in recorded no operator delete 0x1004249a call; the replay records one for odd flags (distinct 10). Seven sibling destructors on the same fixture in the same boot record it live. Both are the ones that reach their class destructor through an incremental-link thunk (0x10001816, 0x10001e06) before the delete call.
column5: Re-run the two keys live with SIMGOLF_HOOKS_OFF for their class-destructor callees and compare the free log.

column4: S4.1: process state the live sound.dll got from Windows is modelled: TlsAlloc's first index 27 (measured: the only value in 0..1099 that reproduces _errno_a's CSV hash; 4 keys observe it), RTL_CRITICAL_SECTION after InitializeCriticalSection (DebugInfo -1, LockCount -1, the rest 0; the SpinCount flags Windows stores are not modelled), CreateEvent / HeapCreate handle numbers, GetVersion 6.2 build 9200. A key whose regions hold one of these values would differ; none in the census does except through the TLS index.
column5: Read the values a live process gets (one Frida session at the menu: TlsGetValue index in sound.dll's __tlsindex, a fresh critical section's bytes).

column4: S4.1: uninitialised inputs differ from the live run: registers are 0 at each call and the stack below esp holds what earlier emulated calls left (zero at first), HeapAlloc / VirtualAlloc blocks are zero; live they held the rpc thread's and the heap's leftovers. A function that reads such a slot can give another result; no census row is attributed to it.
column5: A key that disagrees only on a vector reading uninitialised stack would show it; c3ea's seeded-slot method can pin those slots in both runs.

column4: S4.1: locale and code-page functions (GetACP, GetCPInfo, GetStringTypeA/W, LCMapStringA/W, CompareStringA/W, GetLocaleInfoA/W, Multi/WideChar conversions, IsProcessorFeaturePresent) are answered by the Windows of the PC running the replay; the live runs used the game PC's. A different system locale or code page would change the CRT's ctype tables DllMain builds.
column5: Record GetACP / GetOEMCP / the user LCID on the PCs that ran the C3 rounds.

column4: S4.1: Unicorn 2.1.4 sets no x87 exception flag (PE, IE, SF, ES read 0 after an inexact or invalid fistp and after a stack underflow) and fistp of an empty register stores 0 instead of the integer indefinite 0x8000000000000000; it does apply the precision control (24 / 53 / 64 bits measured). c3fo's __ftol_snd keys: 42 rows per key match only with the status flag byte set (0x20 or 0x01, the SDM's flags), 2 rows (empty st(0)) differ on return and state.
column5: A port judged on fnsave images needs another reference (the flag-byte search, or a softfloat x87 model checked against these CSVs).

column4: S4.1: Memory.alloc is modelled as zero-filled, 16-byte aligned below one page and page aligned (with a guard page) from one page up; Frida's own allocator placement and initial contents are not known. Fixtures fill their blocks; a function sensitive to a block's alignment or to unfilled bytes would differ.
column5: Read gum's Memory.alloc for the round's Frida version.

column4: S4.1: sound.dll's globals at the menu are reproduced only as far as DllMain (the CRT start-up): the game's own calls into sound.dll before the keys (initSound with no device, the sound timer on a PC with a device) are not replayed. Only 5 keys change when DllMain is skipped (log/roadmap/S4/1_census_noinit.tsv); no census disagreement is attributed to a later global.
column5: If a port comparison meets a global the fixture did not set, read it from a live session at the menu.
